math_code.why: Code generation checked by running it (execution accuracy), but in SQL over a given database schema rather than Python with pandas/numpy libraries.

agentic.why: different skill: no tool calls, one query output

datasets.questions_where: https://huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/spider (train/dev; test set and the 200 databases from https://yale-lily.github.io/spider)
datasets.summary: Spider 1.0 (2018): 10,181 English questions over 200 databases, the model writes a SQL query that is executed and compared with the gold result. A related code skill (data querying) with an executed checker, but SQL not Python, old and heavily trained on; the leaderboard is closed since Feb 2024. The Hugging Face rows hold only question, query and db_id: database files and schemas must be fetched from the Spider site.

datasets.name: BIRD-SQL

chat.why: different skill: write an SQL query over a database, not a short text answer

math_code.why: Code generation graded by executing it (result-set match), but in SQL over 95 real databases instead of Python; the prompt must carry the database schema (not in the question rows), so it is likely far longer than Yugos math_code prompts (not measured here).

agentic.why: Not function calling: one question -> one SQL query; only its BIRD-Interact spin-off is an agentic, multi-turn version

datasets.summary: Text-to-SQL: a natural-language question plus an 'evidence' hint over one of 95 large databases (37+ domains); the model writes SQL, graded by execution accuracy. Related to the data-wrangling side of ds1000 but in SQL with long schema prompts; train (9,428) and dev (1,534) are public, test is hidden; a revised dev set (bird_sql_dev_20251106) and a corrected Mini-Dev (Oct 2026) are on Hugging Face.

datasets.name: AssistantBench

chat.why: Short real-life information questions with a short answer and partial-credit scoring (like hotpotqa F1), but they are meant to be solved by browsing current websites, so closed-book answers are mostly wrong or stale.

math_code.why: different skill: web information seeking

agentic.why: Multi-step tool use, but live web browsing over many pages and graded on the final answer, not tools given in the prompt or an end state.

datasets.questions_where: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AssistantBench/AssistantBench (answers only for the 33 dev tasks; 181 test answers hidden)
datasets.summary: AssistantBench (Jul 2024): 214 realistic, time-consuming web tasks (e.g. which of a person's social accounts has most followers) with short answers scored with partial credit; only 33 dev answers are public. Hard and noisy for Yugos: it needs a live browser, answers drift with the web, and even GPT-5 with a browser agent gets 35%. HAL has encrypted traces for 15 model runs; whether they hold per-task scores was not checked.

datasets.name: SWE-bench Verified

chat.why: different skill: repository bug fixing with tools, not a question with a short answer

math_code.why: Python coding checked by hidden unit tests (FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS), but it is patching a whole repo from a GitHub issue over many tool steps, not writing one function from one prompt.

agentic.why: Multi-step agent work (bash/edit tools in a Docker repo) graded on end state by tests, matching the private guess in shape, but a software-engineering domain with no user conversation or business APIs and very long contexts; issues date from before 2024 and are heavily trained on.

datasets.results_where: https://github.com/SWE-bench/experiments
datasets.summary: 500 human-validated GitHub issue + gold patch pairs from popular Python repositories. Graded by running the repo's tests after the agent's patch. Per-instance resolved lists and logs are public for many submissions (SWE-bench/experiments plus submitters' repos). Useful mainly as a hard, end-state-graded agentic prior; its coding-agent domain and context length are far from Yugos's tool-calling questions. It is a Yugos catalog set, not in the live pack.

datasets.name: SWE-bench Verified mini

chat.why: different skill: repository bug fixing with tools, not a question with a short answer

math_code.why: Same as SWE-bench Verified (repo patching checked by tests) but only Django and Sphinx issues, so narrower Python domains.

agentic.why: Multi-step coding agent graded on end state by tests; same shape as the full Verified set but only 50 tasks from 2 repos.

datasets.results_where: https://github.com/SWE-bench/experiments
datasets.summary: A 50-task subset of SWE-bench Verified (Django and Sphinx only; ~5 GB of environments instead of 130 GB) chosen to match the full set's difficulty spread. Per-instance outcomes come from the Verified submissions, because these are the same instance ids. A cheap way to run a hard agentic prior, but too small and too far from Yugos's tool-calling questions to be much training data. It is a Yugos catalog set, not in the live pack.
datasets.level_note: The card says the 50 were picked (k-means + linear programming, 16 models) to keep about the same performance, test pass rate and difficulty distribution as SWE-bench Verified. Copied from our row 11.1 measured scores (GPT-3.5 0.004; Claude 3.5 Sonnet/GPT-4o 0.511; GPT-5/Opus 4.5/Gemini 3 Pro 0.759). Level 4 is unknown, so it is set equal to level 3.

datasets.name: GAIA

chat.why: Short questions with one unambiguous exact answer (like simpleqa/hle), but most need web browsing, code or attached files to answer, so a tool-less one-shot answer is a different task.

math_code.why: different skill: web/file research questions, little math or code writing

agentic.why: Multi-step tool use (browser, code, file readers) graded by exact final answer, not by end state or call AST; no simulated user or business APIs; some questions need image/audio files.

datasets.results_where: https://hal.cs.princeton.edu/gaia
datasets.summary: 466 general-assistant questions in 3 levels (165 validation with public answers; test answers private), each with one short exact answer that needs web search, code and sometimes an attached image/audio/document. Gated: you must accept terms not to reshare it. Agent scores depend heavily on the scaffold (Claude Sonnet 4.5 0.75 vs 0.31 on HAL). HAL says it shares full, encrypted traces of its runs (32 validation runs of 2025 models); no GPT-4o or 2026 score was found. A weak stand-in for Yugos: the router sees text only, and these tasks need browsing.

3.model: GPT-5 Medium with HAL Generalist Agent, 165 validation questions (HF Open Deep Research scaffold: 0.628)

datasets.name: DSBench

chat.why: questions answered from long financial-modelling briefs plus data files and judged by GPT-4o: much longer and more tool-bound than chat questions

math_code.why: Data analysis like ds1000's domain, but the input is a ~815-word brief plus Excel/CSV files and the answer is a value judged by GPT-4o (analysis) or a Kaggle-style submission scored against a baseline (modelling), not code run against tests.

agentic.why: Built for data-science agents that run code over files over many steps (AutoGen, Code Interpreter), so it resembles a multi-step tool task, but there are no function schemas and the grade is a final answer, not an end state.

datasets.results_where: https://github.com/LiqiangJing/DSBench/tree/main/data_analysis (save_process/gpt-3.5-turbo-0125: one model only)
datasets.licence: non-commercial use only (README disclaimer); LICENSE file not read
datasets.summary: 466 data-analysis questions (38 ModelOff financial-modelling challenges, with Excel files; 5 images in total) and 74 Kaggle data-modelling tasks. It is an agent benchmark: the model reads long briefs and data files and works with code; text-mostly but tool-heavy, and only one model's per-task results are published.

chat.why: Open-ended instruction/chat prompts (Alpaca-GPT4, Dolly-15k, GPT4All-LAION, ShareGPT) scored by BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore against a reference and by ChatGPT pairwise comparison, not short checkable answers.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools or function schemas in the prompt

datasets.results_where: https://huggingface.co/datasets/llm-blender/mix-instruct

datasets.name: WildBench per-task eval results

chat.why: Real-user open-ended requests (27% multi-turn) scored 1-10 by a GPT-4o checklist judge with no reference answer, unlike Yugos's exact/MC/F1 chat items.

math_code.why: About a quarter is coding/math help (Coding & Debugging 170, Math 87) but open-ended and judge-scored, not boxed answers or unit tests.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools

datasets.summary: 1,024 WildChat tasks (Info seeking 182, Coding 170, Creative 146, Reasoning 133, Planning 116, Math 87, Editing 82, ...; 748 single-turn, up to 9 turns) with per-task checklists. Per-task results: model output plus GPT-4o judge score (1-10) for ~63 models, and pairwise rewards vs GPT-4-Turbo/Claude-3-Haiku/Llama-2-70B; newest models are mid-2024 (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5, Llama 3 70B, Mistral Large 2); repo last updated 2024-08-01. No tokens, cost or correctness. Weak router signal for the very easy private chat part only.
